title: A Choir for the Salt
premise: Orsen Delacroix, gatekeeper of a sealed threshold between the mortal city of Vell and the drowned realm of Salt, has spent a decade hiding their small magic among charm-sellers while the city's Wardens hunt practitioners. When a dying courier leaves them a map to the covenant-stone binding both realms, Orsen learns the seal they guard is starving the last dragon-fire that keeps Salt from flooding into the world—and that the Wardens' founder built the law to hide his own theft of the flame. Gathering a found family of outcast magicians, Orsen must reach the stone, reforge the broken covenant by surrendering their own hidden power, and choose justice outside the law: exposing the founder's crime at the cost of their own anonymity. The book ends with the covenant renewed, the dragon-fire shared rather than hoarded, and Orsen finally visible—beloved, implicated, and home.
about_author: Xanthe Thackeray is the pen name of a former tide-pool surveyor who spent six years cataloguing coastal folklore before turning to fantasy. They write in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where the sea dictates most of their deadlines.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Would Not Die
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A dying stranger collapses in Orsen's charm stall, pressing a salt-stained map and a warning about 'the guttering' before dissolving into brine. Orsen hides the map as Wardens sweep the market. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant responsibility—the first crack in ten years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Warden-scribe Ilsa Vane, who discovers records proving her order's founder stole the dragon-fire and wrote the magic ban to conceal it. She defects to find Orsen. Meanwhile Orsen recruits exiled hedge-witch Maren and mute fire-dancer Kesh. Emotional beat: the slow, dangerous trust of strangers becoming allies.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The party descends through the gate into drowning Salt, where the last dragon lies guttering like a candle and the covenant-stone demands a life's magic as payment. Wardens ambush them; Kesh burns herself out holding the passage open. Emotional beat: grief and fury—the price of survival made brutally literal.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Salt
chapters.summary: Shared POV between Orsen and Ilsa. At the stone, Orsen surrenders their hidden power while Ilsa reads the founder's crime aloud to both realms, letting the crowd's voices—not one sacrifice—reforge the covenant. The dragon-fire spreads through many keepers. Emotional beat: hard-won resolution; justice beyond law, family beyond blood, visibility beyond fear.
